source.title: Explicit Regularization in Overparametrized Models via Noise Injection
source.authors: Antonio Orvieto; Anant Raj; Hans Kersting; F. Bach

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplementary material, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a different explicit regularization method—noise injected into model parameters before gradient computation—changes held-out performance in overparameterized networks.
record.gate_note: Reports held-out performance under layer-wise and all-parameter noise injection. The measured outcomes concern explicit regularization generally, but do not test a listed version’s specific intervention or measure.
record.test_reason: The study tests parameter-noise regularization, which none of V1–V8 names. Its width comparisons do not establish behavior beyond an interpolation threshold, and its Hessian traces are neither magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance nor rankings of generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: the authors derive explicit regularizers from small parameter perturbations, show how layer-wise perturbations avoid variance explosion under their analyzed conditions, and report improved accuracy in their experiments. They leave a detailed theoretical account of the deep-network regularizer's generalization properties for future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses parameter-noise injection before gradient computation as an explicit regularizer; the listed versions concern other interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer-wise versus simultaneous perturbation, noise scale, and network width change the reported outcome.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-wise parameter noise improves held-out performance in the tested MLPs and CNNs; on ResNet18 the reported gain is approximately 0.3 percentage points. Simultaneous noise can impair convergence or accuracy at larger widths or noise scales.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Perturbing one parameter group at a time before gradient computation can improve generalization and avoid the variance explosion associated with simultaneous parameter perturbations.

fits_no_version.finding: The study compares unscaled Hessian trace with test performance, including oscillatory traces in convolutional networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter-noise regularization can change Hessian trace and held-out performance; this does not establish that magnitude-aware sharpness ranks generalization gaps.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2023)
record.problems: Several principal results are presented in figures without exact values in the text. The ResNet18 comparison reports mean and standard error over only 3 runs. The paper states that convolutional-network effects are less pronounced in the tested narrow network setting.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately stated held-out outcomes were omitted. Other plots show trajectories without text giving exact values; they are represented only where the text explicitly describes the result.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its held-out comparison with natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error, with convergence established.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions, small-data failures, excessive dropout and removal alongside weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, not denials of the reported noise-injection effects. The study cites original sources concerning dropout and sharpness, but its own results do not test those versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and comparison with natural-label generalization.
Test-error behavior when width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization under the version’s comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of train-test gaps against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: MLP with 2 hidden layers (5000 neurons each) and ReLU activations
rows.stage_stated: trained on 1024 Fashion MNIST training examples
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent with layer-wise parameter noise; test accuracy compared across noise scales and standard noise injection.

conditions.value: Fashion MNIST; training subset 1024; test set 10K

rows.value: Figure only; text states layer-wise perturbation can increase test accuracy, in contrast to standard noise injection.
rows.note: The text reports the direction of the result but gives no exact accuracy values.
rows.check: This is performance of the study's proposed regularizer, not a test of a listed version. Section 5 and Figure 3 specify two hidden layers; Appendix F.1 specifies three for the related shallow-wide experiment, so these experiments should not be conflated.

rows.subject: ReLU MLP with 6 layers (5 hidden), width 5000
rows.stage_stated: trained on a subset of Fashion MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent with layer-wise noise or noise on all parameters.
rows.value: Figure only; text states layer-wise perturbations yield improved test accuracy in the overparameterized setting.
rows.note: The figure also plots Hessian trace; exact test-accuracy values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: This compares parameter-noise methods at fixed width, not post-interpolation widening or magnitude-aware sharpness. The training subset contains 1024 examples. Appendix F reports three runs with mean and one standard deviation, so uncertainty is not wholly unstated.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 for 150 epochs; noise stopped at epoch 135
rows.baseline: SGD baseline reaches around 94.4% test accuracy
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard error of the mean over 3 runs; numerical error bars not stated.
rows.note: The paper reports the improvement in prose and plots final test accuracy.
rows.check: This is performance of the proposed regularizer, outside the listed versions. The reported improvement is approximately 0.3 percentage points over the approximately 94.4% SGD baseline; it does not establish any listed effect.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 for 150 epochs; noise stopped at epoch 135
rows.operation_detail: SGD with noise injected in all parameters simultaneously.
rows.baseline: SGD baseline reaches around 94.4% test accuracy
rows.value: For σ>0.1, noise injection hurts performance.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard error of the mean over 3 runs; numerical error bars not stated.
rows.note: The text says simultaneous noise improves test accuracy only for very small σ and hurts for σ>0.1.
rows.check: Higher simultaneous parameter noise hurts accuracy, but this is not a reversal of any listed version. It is a comparator for the study's proposed method.

rows.subject: Fully convolutional network with up to 128 channels
rows.size_stated: 4 convolutional layers with 128 channels and one linear layer
rows.operation_detail: SGD with layer-wise noise compared with noise injected into all weights.
rows.baseline: SGD with noise injected into all weights
rows.value: Text states layer-wise noise provides improved performance in terms of test loss over standard noise injection.
rows.note: No exact test-loss values are stated in the text.
rows.check: This compares noise-injection methods, not a listed intervention. Correct the convolutional channels to 32, 64, 128, 128, followed by a linear layer. Appendix F.2 describes improved test loss, but Figure 12 displays training loss, test accuracy and Hessian trace; it supplies no plotted test-loss value. Appendix F reports three runs with mean and one standard deviation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
